patch.value: The canonical spelling the output contract tells agents to adopt returns every row with every field stripped, and only the one surface that validates its selectors refuses it

The universal read-output layer folds two unrelated kinds of legacy flag into one canonical option. Value-bearing aliases (--fields, --section) name row fields. Mode aliases (--brief, --compact, --full, --summary, --counts, --collapse) name a whole declared projection. Both are mapped to a bare token by flagSelector(), both are advertised through the same emitted migration hint, and only the first kind was ever implemented.

applyIncludeProjection treats every canonical token as a field name. A mode token matches no field, so projectRecordFields returns an empty object for every row. The envelope is not corrected: projection.fields still declares the field list that was removed, count still reports the row count, and the process exits 0.

Measured at HEAD build 2026.8.13, over the 18 (surface, declared mode) pairs reachable from the contract table:

  surface     modes probed   rows emptied   exit
  list        3              5 of 5         0
  search      2              5 of 5         0
  contracts   2              131 of 131     0
  validate    1              9 of 9         0
  history     1              5 of 5         0
  activity    1              5 of 5         0
  get         1              none           2

10 of 18 pairs return the requested row count as empty objects. The single surface that refuses is get, because applyGetIncludeProjection enumerates its legal selectors and throws; every other surface has no enumeration and therefore no refusal.

Two properties make this worse than an ordinary projection bug.

The tool recommends the broken spelling itself. The receipt on a legacy invocation emits 'compatibility alias; prefer --output-include brief'. An agent that follows the hint the tool just printed receives rows with no content and no error. The hint is asserted in tests/fixtures/contracts/full.json as a string and executed nowhere, so the recommendation was frozen while the behaviour behind it never existed.

The affected surfaces include the orientation path. pm contracts is where AGENTS.md routes an agent to discover exact flag contracts; --output-include full empties all 131 rows of it. pm validate --output-include counts empties the governance counts. A caller cannot distinguish this from a workspace that holds nothing.

The root cause is ordering, not vocabulary: a projection mode selects which fields the command computes, so it can only be honoured before the command runs, while the output layer runs after. Mode tokens have to be handed back to the command that owns them.

Every include-dimension migration hint that recommends a bare token resolves that token to the projection mode its legacy alias owns, on every read surface that declares it; A canonical include request is byte-identical to the legacy alias it replaces for all 16 declared (surface, mode) pairs, excluding only the receipt that records which spelling was used; A selector that matches no field on any returned row is refused with the exit code and legal domain the get surface already uses, instead of returning rows with no fields and exit 0; A test executes every emitted migration hint rather than pinning its text, so a recommendation that stops working fails CI; The MCP action path and the CLI path resolve a mode token identically

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Evidence: shipped. applyReadOutputIncludeModes and readOutputIncludeModeOptions added to src/sdk/read-output-contracts.ts split canonical include tokens into declared projection modes and residual field selectors, deriving the mode set from the surface's own include legacy_aliases minus the two value-bearing ones. Both dispatch paths forward consumed modes to the command before it computes rows: src/cli/main.ts writes them back through Commander (the resolved-global cache is cleared and re-read before the handler runs, so stripping only the local copy was not enough) and src/sdk/runtime.ts mirrors it for MCP actions. rejectEmptyIncludeProjection now refuses any projection that strips every field from every row, with the exit code and legal-domain wording get already used.

Verification, all 16 declared (surface, mode) pairs: canonical output is byte-identical to the legacy alias after removing the receipt that records which spelling was used. list brief/compact/full, search compact/full, get full, history compact/full, activity compact/full, contracts full/summary, validate counts, deps full/summary, events full. Before the change 10 of 18 probed pairs returned the requested row count as empty objects with exit 0.

Refusals now teach: 'pm context --output-include brief' returns exit 2 naming that context declares no projection modes; 'pm list --output-include nosuchfield' returns exit 2 naming brief, compact, full. Field selectors are unchanged ('--output-include id,title'), and a mixed request composes correctly (mode applied first, then field narrowing).

Full suite green: 7,272 tests across 491 files. sdk/public-surface.json regenerated; both new symbols classify as contract_data, so the primitives are publicly reachable from the SDK.

value.text: A compatibility layer that maps two different kinds of flag onto one canonical option inherits the obligation to implement both kinds. Here flagSelector() reduced --brief and --fields to the same shape — a bare token — while only one of them was ever a field name, and the difference was invisible because both spellings type-check as a selector string. The tell was that exactly one surface refused: get enumerates its legal selectors, so it could tell a mode from a field; every other surface had no enumeration and therefore no refusal. A layer that cannot enumerate its own legal domain cannot detect the case it does not handle.

patch.value: Canonical --output-include projection modes now resolve to the command-local projection they alias on every declared read surface, verified byte-identical to the legacy flag across all 16 (surface, mode) pairs, and a projection that would strip every field from every row is refused with the legal domain instead of returning empty rows and exit 0. Both the CLI and MCP dispatch paths forward modes identically, and tests/unit/sdk/read-output-migration-hints.spec.ts executes every emitted hint rather than pinning its text.

Split the canonical include dimension into declared projection modes and residual field selectors; modes are forwarded to the owning command before it computes rows, and an all-empty projection is refused with the surface's legal domain.
pm list --output-include brief returns the same rows as pm list --brief, and an unrecognised selector is refused.
All 16 declared (surface, mode) pairs are byte-identical to their legacy flag; unrecognised selectors exit 2 naming the declared modes; full suite green at 7,272 tests.
